author: sjm41
body:
* **InterPro ID / label**
IPR008901 Alkaline ceramidase

* **Example sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Drosophila 'bwa' (Q9VIP7)

* **Description of issue**
IPR008901 is annotated with "[hydrolase activity, acting on carbon-nitrogen (but not peptide) bonds, in linear amides (GO:0016811)](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/GTerm?id=GO:0016811)", to reflect the comment "This entry consists of several ceramidases."
But the entry is only supported by a single reference (PMID: [11356846](https://europepmc.org/abstract/MED/11356846) that is specifically about the mammalian enzyme.
The single fly orthology of the mammalian enzyme ('bwa' (Q9VIP7)) lacks ceramidase activity (see PMID: 21148295) - I'm not sure about other taxa.

I'm not sure if this is sufficient reason to remove the current GO:0016811 annotation - what do you think?
title: IPR008901 Alkaline ceramidase

author: blazaropinto
body:
Hi Steven,
Thank you very much for that. Indeed the ceramidase activity in proteins from this family has been only reported for mammals and yeast in not very recent papers. There is no experimental evidence in plant sequences from this group. And there is evidence in flies in the opposite direction. Therefore, I removed this term and updated the description with this information. The changes will be available in InterPro 107.0.
Best,
Beatriz
